item.observed: Stored order contains kit_id and totals but no line items or quantities.
item.title: Customers' confirmed orders lose the fireworks they bought — checkout sends only a kit ID and the order route never copies its cart

item.observed: A $5 request with one $1 drop can be filled to $6 without a second budget check.
item.title: Customers can receive an over-budget kit even when four cues fit — budget fitting runs before the missing cues are added

item.observed: Closing confirmation loses its only view; stored orders have no status or GET route.
item.title: Customers cannot recover their confirmed order or its delivery progress — the server stores no status and provides no order lookup

item.observed: A nonexistent kit and arbitrary total are stored as a confirmed order.
item.title: The stand can receive orders with fabricated prices or nonexistent kits — POST /api/orders trusts client total_usd and never loads kit_id

item.observed: A fallback kit has 0 source links but still says 'Built from live search'.
item.title: Dancers lose the promised source links when live search fails — the hardcoded trends fallback contains no sources

item.observed: The fallback uses sounds[0] even when the request names another song.
item.title: Dancers get a kit for the wrong song after tapping a trend or naming a track — the catalog fallback always chooses the first cached sound

item.observed: A request without a song gets the first trend rather than 'Your trending track'.
item.title: Dancers without a named song see an unrelated title instead of the requested neutral label — the fallback always picks the first trending sound

item.observed: A passed time such as 00:01 is accepted and the order is confirmed.
item.title: Dancers can schedule deliveries in the past — checkout accepts any nonempty time without a future-time check

item.observed: POST /api/orders accepts an arbitrary spot and non-time text.
item.title: The stand receives orders for invalid landmarks and malformed times — the order schema checks only string length

item.observed: backend/.env has no YDC_API_KEY; without an external override every search uses house picks.
item.title: Dancers get no live You.com trends in the supplied configuration — the requested YDC_API_KEY is absent from backend/.env

item.observed: Both attempts use claude-sonnet-5-5, then return the catalog fallback.
item.title: Dancers lose personalized AI-generated shot plans — both attempts still request the nonexistent Claude model before falling back

item.observed: A 3-second search plus a stalled extraction can delay trends and kit requests for 23 seconds.
item.title: Dancers wait far beyond four seconds for trends and kit generation — the four-second deadline excludes the 20-second extraction

item.observed: Retrying the same payment request after a lost response creates a second order number.
item.title: Customers can create duplicate orders after a checkout retry — the order POST has no idempotency key or deduplication

item.observed: Order numbers use only 24 random bits, and there is no unique index or collision retry.
item.title: Customers can receive another order's number as order volume grows — six random hex digits have no uniqueness constraint

item.observed: A failed /api/trends request renders zero chips and no empty message.
item.title: Dancers lose every trending chip after a network error — the strip replaces the response with empty arrays rather than fallback picks

item.observed: Tapping the same chip twice appends the same text twice with no selected state.
item.title: Dancers duplicate a trend in their request on a second tap — chips have no selection or duplicate guard

item.observed: House picks expire after 60 seconds instead of the requested 10 minutes.
item.title: Dancers get repeated search retries during an outage — fallback results are cached for only one minute

item.observed: A model response with one valid and one invalid cue is accepted without retry.
item.title: Dancers can receive a reconstructed plan missing the model's cues — invalid cue entries are discarded rather than triggering the required retry

item.observed: A $1 drop cue can remain while a $6 non-drop cue is retained.
item.title: Dancers can receive their largest firework away from the beat drop — the planner protects an existing drop cue without comparing the other cues

item.observed: A short model instruction such as 'Play this track' passes through as the song.
item.title: Dancers can still see an instruction in the song field — the changed song cleaner only filters a few forbidden words

item.observed: A $2 limit produces four $1 cues, exceeding the limit by $2 rather than at most $1.
item.title: Dancers with very small budgets receive kits more than one cheapest cue over budget — four unconditional $1 cues can exceed the stated exception

item.observed: Different crew sizes, requested effects and locations get the same five fallback items and tip.
item.title: Dancers lose their requested crew and firework choices when the model fails — the fallback uses one fixed kit regardless of the request

item.observed: An extraction with missing artist/place or an invented title is accepted as live.
item.title: Dancers can see incomplete or invented trends presented as live results — extraction output is not checked against the search results

item.observed: An extraction failure returns house picks with live=true and 'Live · You.com'.
item.title: Dancers mistake fallback songs and events for live trends — extraction failures and empty picks are labeled live

item.observed: When speech synthesis is unavailable the Read aloud button silently does nothing.
item.title: Dancers cannot tell why confirmation speech is silent — the read-aloud handler ignores unavailable or rejected speech and has no error state

item.observed: A request 'budget 80,000 ៛' is parsed as $80,000 rather than $20.
item.title: Dancers using the riel symbol can receive a kit thousands of times over budget — the riel regex requires a word boundary after the non-word currency symbol

item.observed: A fountain item can retain a model description saying 'smoke'.
item.title: Dancers can still receive a cue describing the wrong firework — the changed builder retains the model's unchecked effect text

item.observed: A single drop fountain is drawn as two fountains even when the cart supplies one.
item.title: Dancers still see more fountains in their preview than their cart supplies — the changed effect draws both sides for one drop cue

item.observed: The phone frame has fixed height and max-width but no matching height constraint.
item.title: Dancers on tall narrow phones can still see a stretched 9:16 preview — width is clamped independently of height

item.observed: With drop_second=14 or 15, DROP remains visible after the clock stops at 15.
item.title: Dancers still see DROP stuck over the final preview frame — the label depends on a clock capped before the label can expire

item.observed: Opening preview does not move or trap focus in the full-screen overlay.
item.title: Keyboard users can still activate hidden kit controls behind the preview — the overlay has no dialog semantics or focus management

item.observed: A fountain cue at second 15 is queued and removed before it emits any particles.
item.title: Dancers miss a fountain, smoke or spinner on a 15-second drop — the new end-of-timeline cleanup removes its emitter before its first tick

item.observed: Closing the dialog during POST can hide a successfully created order and its number.
item.title: Customers can lose their order confirmation while checkout is pending — the dialog remains dismissible while the order POST continues

item.observed: A one-result search produces one source; duplicate URLs remain duplicated.
item.title: Dancers can get too few distinct Why this kit sources — search results are neither deduplicated by URL nor padded to two links

item.observed: Drop particle size is 1.6×, and fountain velocity is √3× rather than 3×.
item.title: Dancers still do not see a three-times-larger drop effect — the changed director and effects apply smaller scale factors

item.observed: A cue at 0 can fire while readyRef is false, before beat.play starts.
item.title: Dancers can still miss synchronization of a zero-second cue — the director fires at time zero before scene readiness starts the beat

item.observed: At 0:15 the timeline freezes but lights and camera controls continue updating.
item.title: Dancers still see the final preview frame changing after 15 seconds — light decay and orbit updates continue after the clock is capped

item.observed: The 2D fallback receives no mode or pointer handler and renders one fixed viewpoint.
item.title: Dancers without WebGL still cannot orbit or see the phone perspective — the changed fallback ignores view mode and dragging

item.observed: The preview still exposes Replay but no Pause control.
item.title: Dancers still cannot pause the preview to inspect a cue — the changed timeline advances continuously and has no pause state

item.observed: The changed card offers preview and order but no share or copy action.
item.title: Dancers still cannot copy or share their plan with a crew — the changed kit card provides no share or copy control

item.observed: An unbroken song or filming-tip word can extend beyond the card's clipped edge.
item.title: Phone users can still lose long generated song or filming text — the changed kit card clips unbreakable text

item.observed: A fallback request for a drop at 15 seconds is returned with drop_second=14.
item.title: Dancers get the fallback firework at the wrong time for a 15-second drop — the fallback parser clamps every requested drop to 14

item.observed: The spoken confirmation does not mention Packed, On the tuk-tuk, or Arrived.
item.title: Dancers relying on spoken confirmation do not hear a delivery status — the utterance omits every status step

item.observed: The mock-payment POST stores no payment status or mock-paid marker.
item.title: The stand cannot distinguish mock-paid orders from unpaid ones — checkout stores no payment state

item.observed: Long trend titles and artists are truncated at 200px with no way to expand them.
item.title: Phone users cannot identify long trend titles or artists before choosing a chip — both lines are truncated without a full-text view

item.observed: After a failed rebuild the prior card remains without its originating request or stale label.
item.title: Dancers can still mistake an old kit for their failed new request — the changed build handler retains the previous card without a stale label

item.observed: A pending rebuild can replace the kit prop while an old kit's checkout is open.
item.title: Dancers can order a different kit than the one they selected — checkout reads the live card prop while an earlier rebuild can replace it

item.observed: A build that finishes during preview replaces kit data without resetting fired cue indices.
item.title: Dancers can still see a mixed or incomplete preview when a new build finishes — the changed timeline retains old fired cues while its kit prop changes

item.observed: A chip appended to a 2000-character request exceeds the limit and POST returns 422.
item.title: Dancers with long requests cannot build after adding a trend — chip insertion bypasses the input's 2000-character limit

item.observed: The landmark step shows neither total before Continue to pay.
item.title: Customers must advance to the payment card to review their bill — the delivery step omits the kit totals

item.observed: The footer uses small slate-500 text against the dark sky, below 4.5:1 contrast.
item.title: Dancers can struggle to read the new footer — its small slate-500 text has insufficient contrast on the dark background

item.observed: With a $6 drop and $8 budget, the planner replaces the drop rather than returning $9.
item.title: Dancers can lose their selected drop firework despite the allowed small budget exception — the changed planner swaps the protected drop to a cheaper item

item.observed: Two 60-second model timeouts can delay a fallback kit for over two minutes.
item.title: Dancers can be left waiting over two minutes for a fallback kit — both model attempts each consume a full 60-second timeout

item.observed: Landmark buttons change color but do not expose a selected or pressed state.
item.title: Screen-reader users cannot tell which delivery landmark is selected — the spot buttons expose no selected state

item.observed: Reloading after an order resets the landmark and generates a new default time.
item.title: Repeat customers must re-enter their delivery details after a reload — the last landmark and time exist only in component state
